test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which type of coal has the highest percentage of carbon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthracite.**__

__
 
• **Anthracite is the best quality of coal with the highest calorific value and has a carbon content of 80 to 95%**__.

 __
 
• It ignites slowly with a blue flame and is found in small quantities in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is a very low volatile substance.
 
• This is a negligible ratio of moisture.
 
• Semi-metallic luster.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The rank of coal is based on the amount of the plant converted into carbon. Based on this four types of coal are generated:-
 
 
• Anthracite
 
• Bituminous
 
• Lignite
 
• Peat
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bituminous**

 
 
• It is soft coal; the most widely available and used coal.
 
• Derives its name after a liquid called bitumen.
 
• Contains 40 to 80 % Carbon.
 
• Moisture and volatile content.
 
 
 
• **Lignite**
 
 
• It is a Brown Coal.
 
• Lower-grade coal.
 
• Contains 40 to 55% carbon.
 
• Dark to black-brown.
 
• It undergoes Spontaneous combustion.
 
 
 
• ​**Peat**
 
 
• The first stage of transformation.
 
• Contains less than 40 to 55% carbon.
 
• Contains sufficient volatile matter and a lot of moisture.
 
• It burns like wood, gives less heat, emits more smoke and leaves a lot of ash.
